title: Matrix exponential and phi function actions

items.title: The phi-function family by everywhere-convergent series
items.statement: For every nonnegative integer k, define scalar and finite-matrix phi_k by the series sum of z^j/(j+k)! and X^j/(j+k)!, with phi_0 equal to the scalar or matrix exponential and phi_k(0)=1/k!.

items.title: The Euclidean logarithmic norm of a complex matrix
items.statement: For A in C^(n x n), n>=1, define mu_2(A)=lambda_max((A+A*)/2), where A* is the conjugate transpose and lambda_max is the largest real eigenvalue of the Hermitian part.

items.title: Normwise certified matrix-vector and vector-step arithmetic
items.statement: A certified Taylor arithmetic provider returns each scaled matrix-vector term and vector sum together with a verified nonnegative rational upper bound for its Euclidean-norm local error; a missing bound is an inconclusive result.

items.title: Variation of constants for a finite-matrix action defect
items.statement: If u is a continuously differentiable approximate trajectory for x'=Ax and r(t)=Au(t)-u'(t), then exp(tA)v-u(t)=exp(tA)(v-u(0))+the oriented integral from 0 to t of exp((t-s)A)r(s) ds for positive or negative time.

items.title: The scalar and matrix phi series converge absolutely
items.statement: For every k>=0 and every scalar z or finite square matrix X over C, the defining phi_k series converges absolutely; its values at zero are 1/k! and I/k!.

items.title: The Euclidean logarithmic norm is a real Rayleigh-quotient maximum
items.statement: For A in C^(n x n), n>=1, the Hermitian part has real eigenvalues and mu_2(A)=max_{||x||_2=1} Re<x,Ax>.

items.title: Finite scaled Taylor action for the matrix exponential
items.statement: Given rational certified upper bounds rho_A>=||A||_2, rho_t>=|t| and rho_v>=||v||_2, positive tolerance and finite scaling/order budgets, select s,p with rational R=rho_t rho_A/s<=1, evaluate s degree-p Taylor actions using certified local matvec and vector-step errors, and return a normwise truncation-plus-roundoff bound or an inconclusive status.

items.title: Phi recurrence and augmented-matrix action identities
items.statement: For every k>=0, z and square matrix X, phi_k(z)=1/k!+z phi_(k+1)(z) and phi_k(X)=I/k!+X phi_(k+1)(X); a single augmented exponential has top-right block phi_k(X)w for every vector w, including k=1 without division at zero.

items.title: The logarithmic norm bounds forward and reverse matrix exponentials
items.statement: For every A in C^(n x n) and tau>=0, ||exp(tau A)||_2<=exp(tau mu_2(A)); applying the same result to -A bounds negative time.

items.title: Scaled Taylor action has a finite normwise truncation and roundoff certificate
items.statement: For R<=1 and degree p, the Taylor tail is bounded by q_p(R)=R^(p+1)/((p+1)!(1-R/(p+2))); s steps yield a total truncation bound s*3^(s-1)q_p(R)||v|| and certified local roundoff adds sum_l 3^(s-l) epsilon_l, with exactly s*p calls to A.

items.title: Arnoldi projection for exponential and phi-function actions
items.statement: Run Arnoldi for at most m steps and return beta V_j phi_k(tH_j)e_1, evaluating the reduced action by the augmented identity and finite Taylor action. Report Arnoldi breakdown, relation certification, reduced-action certification, and final-projection certification separately; happy-breakdown requires exact invariance, while an uncertified small computed subdiagonal is numerical-breakdown.

items.title: Arnoldi action error is the semigroup-weighted residual integral
items.statement: The exponential-action error equals the variation-of-constants integral of the Arnoldi defect; logarithmic-norm control bounds it, and certified matvec, orthogonalization, initial-vector, reduced-exponential, and final-projection errors enter additively. Exact invariant-subspace data give exact phi actions.

title: Matrix exponential and phi function actions — Examples

items.title: The value phi_1(0) is obtained directly from its series
items.statement: For the zero 1-by-1 matrix, verify phi_1(0)=1 and the augmented exponential returns the same value without evaluating (exp(z)-1)/z.

items.title: A one-dimensional Arnoldi projection misses a slow mode of a stiff diagonal matrix
items.statement: For A=diag(-100,-1), v=(1,1), t=0.1 and m=1, compute the projected exponential action and compare it exactly with exp(tA)v.

items.title: A nonnormal action grows transiently while its Arnoldi residual certificate remains valid
items.statement: For A=[[-1,3],[0,-1]], v=e_2 and t=1, compute the one-step Arnoldi residual, exact action, logarithmic-norm bound and the resulting action-error certificate.
